scenario: AITA for refusing an additional guest at our wedding | Thanks for watching this post. First time writing here and non-native English speaker. I am getting married very soon. As you can imagine, this takes a lot of preparation. I'm talking here about the civil wedding, which will be very intimate and consequently restricted to our very close family: parents, siblings and, in my case, godparents and their children. The wedding will happen in another country, so this takes a lot of preparation as it is in another culture. When I made the invitations, I've been clear: I invited my parents (2 p.) and my godparents' family (4 p.). I've been very flexible, I told everyone that they could join us anytime they like (i.e., arrive in the country when they wish because I understand it's complicated when you have 4 different jobs etc) as long as they'll be present for the ceremony. Moreover, because the destination is far, my in-laws kindly proposed to offer the accommodation to all of them. The wedding is now in one month and I just received a message from my godmother saying that they have booked the flights, and they will be 5 because the gf of my cousin is joining. That's where I am really feeling uncomfortable: I receive this as a 'fait accompli' (done deal) without any prior consultation, without even asking me if that's ok to have an additional person (that I've never met). I've always been clear about the number of people invited. I just can't stand to receive this kind of 'news' via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against that additional person. It's just the way that I'm put in front of this, as if I had nothing to say. And we're not talking about the 'party' wedding, but something very special that is meant to be in strict intimacy. Moreover, I know that they have their tickets since 1 month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip etc. So they literally waited 1 month to announce it, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything, and to ask if it's possible, etc. In sum, they just invited someone at my wedding, someone that wasn't ever planned and that I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: 'I'm confused by your news, I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e. you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise.' So: Am I the asshole? More precisely: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole for refusing to let an additional guest come to my wedding. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I'm getting married soon, and it's a civil ceremony that's supposed to be very intimate. I've only invited my very close family: my parents, siblings, godparents, and their children. That's a total of 6 people. The wedding is in another country, which means a lot of preparation, especially since it's in a different culture. When I sent out the invitations, I was clear about the number of people I wanted to attend. I told everyone they could come anytime, as long as they were present for the ceremony. I even mentioned that my in-laws would be providing accommodation for everyone since the destination is far away. Now, one month before the wedding, I received a message from my godmother saying that they've booked their flights and that there will be 5 people coming instead of the 4 I had planned. The additional person is the godfather of my cousin, someone I've never met. I was really uncomfortable with this because it felt like a done deal without any prior consultation. They didn't even ask me if it was okay to have an extra person. I've always been clear about the number of guests I wanted, and I couldn't stand receiving this news via a late-night text message. It's not that I'm against having an additional person; it's just the way I was put in front of this decision, as if I had nothing to say. We're not talking about a big party wedding but something very special meant to be strictly intimate. Moreover, I know that they had their tickets booked a month ago, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip and other arrangements. They literally waited a month to announce this, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything and to ask if it's possible. In summary, they just invited someone to my wedding without my knowledge, someone who was never planned and whom I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message expressing my confusion and frustration. I explained that I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests. I asked why they didn't call me and ask before booking anything. I felt like I was put in front of a done deal, and I had to oppose it because it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. Now, the question is: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it won't be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? To determine this, I need to consider a few factors: 1. **Clarity in Communication**: Did I make it clear from the beginning about the number of guests I wanted? It seems like I did, as I mentioned being clear about the number and the specific guests. 2. **Expectation of Consultation**: Is it reasonable to expect that any changes to the guest list would require prior consultation with me? Yes, especially since I was the one planning the event and had specific reasons for the guest list. 3. **Impact on the Event**: Would adding an additional guest significantly impact the intimacy and planning of the wedding? It seems like it would, given that the event is supposed to be very intimate and the additional person was not planned for. 4. **Timing of the Announcement**: Announcing the change a month before the event, after booking flights, seems like poor timing and could be seen as disrespectful to my planning process. 5. **Method of Communication**: Receiving the news via a late-night text message instead of a direct conversation could be seen as dismissive of my feelings and concerns. 6. **My Response**: Did I handle the situation in a respectful and clear manner? It seems like I did, by expressing my confusion and frustration politely and explaining my reasons. Considering these points, it doesn't seem like I'm being an asshole for refusing the additional guest. My concerns are valid, and my communication was respectful. It's reasonable to expect that changes to the guest list would be discussed with me beforehand, especially when it affects the intimacy and planning of the event. However, it's also important to consider the relationship dynamics. If my godmother and her family are close to me, there might be a way to address the issue more diplomatically or to find a compromise that respects both my wishes and their desire to include the additional guest. But given the circumstances, my stance seems justified. In conclusion, I don't think I'm the asshole for refusing the additional guest. My reasons are valid, and my communication was respectful and clear.
